name: Breitenbach am Inn
kurzbeschreibung: Warm and welcoming village of Inn with its Baroque church and the lovely hiking area Breitenbacher Wald.
beschreibung:
Overview

Breitenbach am Inn is a sun-blessed and historic municipality in Tyrol's Kufstein district, situated at roughly 520 meters above sea level in the Lower Inn Valley. Spanning nearly 38 square kilometers along the sunny northern banks of the Inn River opposite Kundl and Wörgl, the town is home to around 3,580 residents across its districts of Breitenbach, Kleinsöll, Schönau, and Haus. Celebrated as the sunniest community in the Lower Inn Valley, it harmoniously blends fertile agricultural meadows and riverside riparian woodlands with the forested slopes of the Brandenberg Alps, culminating at Mount Plessenberg (1,743 m).

History

Breitenbach occupies a paramount position in Tyrolean ecclesiastical history. Following the organization of Bavarian dioceses by Saint Boniface in 739, the Inn River served as the ecclesiastical boundary between Salzburg and Freising for over a thousand years. Breitenbach belonged to the Diocese of Freising and ranks as one of the oldest mother parishes in the Inn Valley, documented as early as 800 AD as an endowment for monks in Kufstein. The community was first recorded in writing in 1157 as Praytenpach. The municipal coat of arms features a pike swimming in a silver wavy bend, recalling the historic bounty of its streams. The parish church dedicated to Saint Peter is acknowledged as the oldest documented parish church in the Tyrolean Unterland. The current Baroque hall church was built between 1737 and 1739 by Georg Hueber incorporating Romanesque and Gothic stone fabric, crowned by an imposing double onion-domed steeple.

How to Get There

By car, visitors easily reach Breitenbach via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Wörgl-West or Kramsach/Brixlegg and following provincial road L211 along the valley floor in a few minutes. Train travelers take advantage of Kundl railway station on the opposite bank of the Inn, accessible via a covered pedestrian bridge within minutes, or the rail junction at Wörgl Hauptbahnhof. Regional VVT bus route 760 connects Wörgl with Breitenbach hourly.

Tips

Nature enthusiasts can explore the Innauen European Nature Reserve, where preserved riparian floodplain forests provide refuge for rare bird species such as grey herons and kingfishers. Cyclists enjoy the paved, level Inn Cycle Path R2 for panoramic rides along the river. A romantic excursion leads to Lake Berglsteiner See, a hidden forest bathing lake nestled between Breitenbach and Kramsach featuring an idyllic lakeside restaurant. Hikers ascend Mount Plessenberg or Aschauer Kreuz to sample alpine cheeses at the Ruhreralm hut. The historic river footbridge also grants immediate walking access to the impressive geological Kundler Klamm gorge.
